resources.string: Bring in your runs and other activities from Garmin Connect

With your own personal API key from Garmin, Flownics brings in each activity you record (the full recording: every lap, pace, heart rate, cadence, step length) into your journal, and matches it to your plan. It only reads, and only your own account.

1. Open the key page in Garmin Connect (signed in to your account).\n2. Create Key, accept Garmin\'s terms, and choose how long it lasts (up to a year).\n3. Copy the key (Garmin shows it only once) and paste it here.

Flownics syncs in the background every few hours when there\'s a network (Android picks the exact time to save battery), and also when you open the journal. The first time it goes 30 days back. Each activity is downloaded once. When the key expires, make a new one and paste it here.
The key is kept encrypted on this phone (Android Keystore), is sent only to Garmin, and isn\'t in backups. Garmin intends the personal key for your own data, not for apps serving others.
Without a key: in Garmin Connect, open an activity, ⋮, Export Original, and import the file in the journal (Import a FIT file).

Step length: about %1$d cm (from speed and cadence)
How much the heart rate rose against the pace from the first half to the second. Under about 5% on a steady easy run is good aerobic endurance; on intervals or a progression run it means little.
The line is the heart rate the watch measured; the shaded bands are your sets, as you started and finished them in the app. Time runs left to right.
Heart rate over the workout, from %1$d to %2$d, with %3$d sets marked.
Zones from your max heart rate %2$d (and resting, if given): %1$s. Set them in What the coach remembers.
Zones from the highest heart rate your recordings measured, %2$d (give your real max in What the coach remembers): %1$s.
Last 7 days %1$d · weekly average over 4 weeks %2$d

Load is minutes in each heart-rate zone times the zone (1–5), from %1$d recordings with heart rate; %2$d without it aren\'t counted. Each bar is a day, oldest left. A ratio well above 1.3 is a sharp jump; below 0.8, a lighter stretch.
Max heart rate taken as %1$d from your recordings.
For heart-rate zones and training load. Without a max, the highest your recordings measured is used.
Live heart rate during workouts in the app

Choose a heart-rate sensor (a chest strap, or your watch broadcasting its heart rate). Every workout in the app then connects to it, shows the live heart rate, and keeps it with the workout: heart rate set by set, zones and load. If the watch also records the workout and it syncs later, its recording takes over.
Garmin: on the watch, turn on Broadcast Heart Rate (in the heart-rate widget\'s menu, or Broadcast During Activity in the sensor settings, depending on the model), then scan here.
Not connected now (it connects when a workout starts)
Without Bluetooth permission the app can\'t look for the sensor. You can allow it in the app\'s Android settings.
